task.description:
Gate CODE-DESIGNER's design artefact at lib/letflow/design/iss-0467-direct-push-prohibition.md. This is a docs/protocol design (no @spec/module interface) -- your bar is: every ISS-0467.yaml acceptance criterion is covered by a concrete design element, the option choice (Option 2, prohibition) is honestly justified against ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis rather than asserted, the exact verbatim text for both GIT_MERGE.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 is unambiguous enough to apply without further judgement calls, no implementation code is present, and the reasoning about ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 (whether the sizing rule as currently written already prohibits a bare push, and whether a correction is still needed) is independently checked against the actual text of sec.10 and AGENT_SYSTEM.md sec.4 -- re-derive this yourself by reading those two sections directly, do not accept CODE-DESIGNER's characterization of them on trust. Also independently verify the claim that Option 1 (GitHub restrictions) is a genuine no-op given the single-identity auth setup -- re-read ISSUE-FIXER's live-verified evidence in step-01-issue-fixer.json directly rather than trusting CODE-DESIGNER's summary of it. Check placement instructions are unambiguous (exact insertion points named). Check AC3's claim that nothing regresses the gh pr merge/--admin path -- verify by reading GIT_MERGE.md's actual Step 8 and confirming the design proposes no edit to it.

REGATE (iteration 1): your prior FAIL (gate_history[0]) found exactly 1 BLOCKER -- design section 7 mislabeled its 3 acceptance criteria as verbatim from docs/issues/ISS-0467.yaml, which has no such field. CODE-DESIGNER's rework (commit 596564c9) retitled section 7 to 'Acceptance criteria mapping (as filed in GitHub issue #896 / this run's task framing)' and added an explicit sourcing note stating ISS-0467.yaml has no acceptance_criteria field, with a matching fix to section 6's echo. Re-verify: (a) confirm this specific correction actually landed as described by reading the current design file yourself, (b) confirm no other section changed (diff the current file's sections 1-6/Open Questions against your own iteration-0 findings -- they should be identical), (c) your other 7 iteration-0 findings do not need to be re-derived from scratch since nothing they depend on changed, but spot-check that the design file's insertion-point text for GIT_MERGE.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 is still byte-identical to what you verified before (the rework should not have touched those quoted blocks).
acceptance_criteria: Every ISS-0467.yaml acceptance criterion (1, 2, 3) mapped to a concrete design element, verified by you reading the design doc's own mapping section AND cross-checking it against the issue file
Option 2 justification re-derived independently: read step-01-issue-fixer.json's actual diagnosis text and confirm it supports the 'no-op' conclusion the design draws from it
ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 and AGENT_SYSTEM.md sec.4 read directly by you; confirm or refute the design's claim that neither currently licenses a bare push to main
GIT_MERGE.md verbatim insertion text and location instructions are unambiguous -- confirm the named insertion point actually exists at the stated location in the current file
ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 verbatim insertion text and location instructions are unambiguous -- confirm the named insertion point actually exists at the stated location in the current file
No implementation code (.ex/.exs bodies) present anywhere in the design artefact
AC3 regression claim verified by reading GIT_MERGE.md Step 8 directly and confirming no edit to it is proposed
Decision-record placement (amend 0018 in place vs new record) reasoning checked against 0018's own 'What this record does not decide' and 'Follow-up' sections

result.summary: Independently re-derived seven of eight checks and they PASS, but one BLOCKER fails the gate. (1) Read step-01-issue-fixer.json's result.summary in full: it live-quotes gh api output showing `restrictions` absent from main's protection response, gh auth status/gh api user/gh api repos permissions showing single identity `tvolodi` with admin:true used for every push and merge, and an explicit factual conclusion that a push-restriction allowlist naming that one identity 'would restrict push access to precisely the one identity that already does everything... making the rule a no-op with respect to distinguishing push classes.' This supports the design's Option-1-is-a-no-op conclusion; no gap found in that reasoning. (2) Read ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 (lines 318-342, confirmed to be the file's final section) and AGENT_SYSTEM.md's actual sizing-rule-exception text at line 95 (sec.4, 'Handoff system' -- NOT the roster section the design's own prose labels 'sec.4' loosely but the correct section per grep of headings). sec.10's opening sentence: 'ORCH may act directly, without spawning the producer/validator chain' -- names the agent chain, not git mechanics; its six-item checklist (one file, no new public API/spec, no migration, no supervision file, no tenant-data path, no test-behavior change) says nothing about push vs. PR. AGENT_SYSTEM.md line 95: 'ORCH may act directly, without spawning a subagent or writing a handoff file, only when a change passes all six checks of ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10's sizing rule' -- same scoping, handoff/subagent machinery only. CONFIRMED: neither section as currently worded licenses a bare `git push origin main`; the design's reading is correct and its proposed corrective sentence is justified given the demonstrated real-world ambiguity (0018's own incident). (3) Confirmed both insertion points exist verbatim as described: GIT_MERGE.md's Precondition paragraph ends '...they also gate the actual merge call itself, not only the meaning of "green" the agent chooses to trust.' (line 29) immediately followed by '**What "reported green" means here.**' (line 31) -- exact match to the design's cited surrounding text. ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10's closing paragraph ends '...When a check is ambiguous, it is a "no."' (line 342), confirmed to be both sec.10's and the entire file's final line -- exact match. (4) Read GIT_MERGE.md Step 8 in full (lines 269-298): the three-path merge procedure (plain merge / PENDING-retry / FAILURE+attribution --admin override) is exactly as 0018 left it; the design proposes no edit to this step anywhere in the document -- AC3 confirmed, no regression. (5) Read docs/issues/ISS-0467.yaml in full (42 lines: id, title, discovered_by/in/at, severity, tags, description, affected_files, related, source, queue_task_id, github_issue, status). BLOCKER FOUND: this file has NO `acceptance_criteria` field and contains none of the three numbered criteria the design's Section 7 ('Acceptance criteria mapping (ISS-0467.yaml, verbatim criteria)') quotes as items 1/2/3 ('Either configure restrictions... or add an explicit line to GIT_MERGE.md...', 'If restrictions are added, live-verify them...', 'No regression to the existing gh pr merge / --admin override path'). Grepped the file for acceptance_criteria/AC1/AC2/AC3/restrictions -- zero matches. Those three criteria text strings actually originate from step-01-issue-fixer.json's task.description and task.acceptance_criteria (the ISSUE-FIXER handoff), not from ISS-0467.yaml itself. The design document misattributes its central compliance section to a source file that does not contain the cited text, labeling it 'verbatim' when it is not verbatim from the named file at all. (6) Confirmed no implementation code: the full design document was read end to end: prose plus quoted Markdown blockquote paragraphs only (the two verbatim insertions for GIT_MERGE.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md); no .ex/.exs bodies, no @spec, no gen_statem shape, no shell/gh commands introduced anywhere. Clean. (7) Read 0018's actual 'A real gap found live' section (lines 460-490, including its 'Follow-up, not re-opening this decision' subsection) and 'What this record does not decide' section (lines 492-508, three exclusions: other-branch protection, a future third required check, automating the override decision -- none is 'whether to prohibit direct pushes'). The design's placement instruction ('append after A real gap found live, before What this record does not decide') matches the actual adjacent section order (grep confirms headings at line 460 then 492, in that order) and its reasoning that this is completing an already-scoped follow-up rather than a new independent design call is well supported by the quoted text. No issue with sections 1, 3, or 4 of the design.

issues.description: Design section 7 ('Acceptance criteria mapping (ISS-0467.yaml, verbatim criteria)') quotes three numbered criteria and labels them verbatim quotes from docs/issues/ISS-0467.yaml. Independently reading ISS-0467.yaml in full confirms it has no `acceptance_criteria` field and contains none of that text anywhere (description/affected_files/related/source/etc. do not mention 'restrictions', 'live-verify', or 'gh pr merge --admin'). The quoted text instead matches step-01-issue-fixer.json's task.description/task.acceptance_criteria (the ISSUE-FIXER handoff, not the issue file). This is a fabricated/misattributed citation in the design's own central compliance-mapping section -- it must be corrected to either (a) cite the actual source of those three criteria (the ISSUE-FIXER handoff's task framing, not ISS-0467.yaml), or (b) if ISS-0467.yaml is intended to carry acceptance criteria, add them there first and then map to the corrected file. As currently written, a downstream agent applying this design cannot verify AC coverage against the issue record itself, which is exactly the ambiguity this gate exists to catch.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework: correct design section 7's citation so it accurately identifies the source of the three 'acceptance criteria' it maps against (they come from step-01-issue-fixer.json's task framing, not from docs/issues/ISS-0467.yaml, which has no acceptance_criteria field at all) -- either retitle/re-source section 7 accurately, or coordinate with REQ-ANALYST/ISSUE owner to add real acceptance_criteria to ISS-0467.yaml and remap. All other sections of the design (Option 2 justification, GIT_MERGE.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 verbatim text and insertion points, AC3/no-regression claim, decision-record placement reasoning, absence of implementation code) independently verified and are correct as written -- do not need rework.
